lesson_topic: Learning Theories — Complementary Lenses: Unifying Learning Paradigms

principles.evidence: No non-decorative graphics, diagrams, charts, or illustrations are present in any of the five slides; all slides consist exclusively of text. The absence of any visual channel means no reciprocity between verbal and visual content can be established, and the multimedia principle is almost entirely unmet.

On-screen text across all slides consists of full paragraphs — three complete sentences per slide — rather than keywords or short phrases. The transcript narration is verbatim or near-verbatim to the on-screen text, with no substantive elaboration or deviation across any slide.

Complex descriptions are delivered via dense on-screen prose rather than narration, with the visual channel carrying no graphics whatsoever. The narration does not read a complex visual aloud (criterion d is met by default as there are no visuals), and the spoken language is moderately natural in register, though it mirrors the on-screen text closely.

No decorative clipart or extraneous imagery is present, satisfying criterion a by default given the text-only format; content stays on-topic with no overt tangential anecdotes. Background and styling appear clean and consistent across slides, though the heavy paragraph-dense text layout introduces a degree of visual noise.

No visual cues such as arrows, highlights, color contrast, or bold text are used to mark key elements, and no captions or callouts are present. The narration includes minimal verbal signaling; slide titles provide a rudimentary hierarchy, but no single key takeaway is explicitly emphasized per slide.

No graphics are present, so label-to-graphic proximity, integrated text, and visual connections between terms and referents cannot be observed or evaluated. Text blocks are not split from associated visuals (criterion c partially met by default), but the principle is structurally inapplicable without any visual elements.
